$comment: Single source of truth for the provider-name maps that used to be kept
by hand in five places: configuration/omniroute/apply.ps1 ($ProviderMap),
configuration/omniroute/apply.sh (PROVIDER_MAP), tools/mirror-litellm-env.py
(KEY_MAP), tools/sync-router-tiers.py (ENV_KEY / PROVIDER_PREFIX / API_BASE)
and the table in docs/api-keys.md.
Entries are keyed by the api-keys.yml name, spelled exactly as the file
spells it. 'SambaNova' keeps its capital S/N on purpose: the mirror tool
looks the key up case-sensitively, so a lower-cased key there would
silently drop the SambaNova key from litellm/.env. apply.ps1/apply.sh
lower-case the api-keys.yml keys as they parse, so they lower-case these
names again on read.
Field meanings:
omniroute_id   the OmniRoute provider id apply registers, or null when
there is nothing to register. 'meta' is null since
2026-09-23: the Meta gateway 502s upstream, no combo leg
references it and routing is openrouter-first; direct
Meta access stays via the opencode meta provider (own
key, own billing). 'omniroute' is null too - it is the
client key apps send, not a provider.
litellm_env    the env-var name the LiteLLM .env / config.yaml use.
litellm_prefix LiteLLM transport prefix when it differs from the
OmniRoute provider id (the OpenAI-compatible gateways
need 'openai'); null to pass the id through unchanged.
api_base       endpoint for the OpenAI-compatible gateways, else null.
provider_data  connection quirks applied at registration, else null.
groq and cerebras sit behind Cloudflare, which answers
error 1010 to Node's default User-Agent; a plain client
UA is accepted.
Order is the order tools/mirror-litellm-env.py emits lines into
litellm/.env. Reordering this file rewrites that file's line order, which
shows up as --check drift, so change it deliberately (see
tests/helpers/check-provider-registry.py, which pins the order).
